tossups.text: The Calypso Deep is the lowest point in this body of water, and Strait of Bonifacio separates two of its larger islands. This sea contains the Balearic Islands, and the Ebro and Rhone rivers flow into it. This sea is connected to the Black Sea via the Bosphorus Strait and to the Atlantic by way of the Strait of Gibraltar. Extensions of this sea include the Aegean and the Adriatic. Containing the islands of Sardinia and Sicily, this sea forms the coastlines of Libya and Algeria. For 10 points, identify this large sea sandwiched between north Africa and Europe.

This Austrian scientist is known for his theory of the Oedipus Complex, where young boys are drawn to their mothers, and for his theory of the "life drive" and "death drive." He may be better known for his theory about the three forces of the psyche - the ego, superego and id - or for his work concerning the interpretation of dreams. For 10 points, name this German psychologist and father of psychoanalysis.

The set designer Oliver Smith became famous following his work for a piece by this composer, during which the railroad song "Sis Joe" introduces a group of characters on horseback. In that work by this composer, "Saturday Night Waltz" and "Hoe-Down" include dances between the Champion Roper and the Cowgirl. Martha Graham and Agnes de Mille choreographed ballets for, for 10 points, what composer, who included "Buckaroo Holiday" in Rodeo, and borrowed from the Shaker song "Simple Gifts" in his work for Appalachian Spring?

In this presidential election, Tennessee Senator Estes Kefauver won the Democratic primary in New Hampshire, leading the sitting Democratic president to withdraw from the race. Robert Taft of Ohio, known as Mr. Republican, was surprisingly defeated by a write-in candidate in the New Hampshire primary; both parties had wooed that write-in candidate while he was serving in Paris as operational commander of NATO forces. For 10 points, Adlai Stevenson first lost to Dwight Eisenhower in what second presidential election after World War II?

The Nsinga and Dema peoples were displaced during the creation of this body of water, whose name comes from the Nyungwe for "finish the job." This body of water runs through a canyon between the Movuradonha (mo-voo-ra-DON-ya) Mountains and the Montes Couesse (koo-ES-say). The Magoe National Park was established by the Tchuma Tchato (CHOO-ma CHA-to) Wildlife Management Program on the south shore of this lake. This body of water extends from the inflow of the Luangua to just above the Capoche (ca-PO-chay) junction at Songo. Electric lines that pass through Pafuri begin at a dam on this lake that supplies the coal mines at Moatize as well as the downstream community of Tete. This lake's level depends on outflow from the upstream Kariba Dam. For 10 points, name this lake created by a namesake dam on the Zambezi River, the largest lake in Mozambique.

It originated from an attempt to help wannabe astronomers make a name for themselves. When it was invented, discovering a comet was the way to become a famous astronomer, but there were many objects that were easily confused with comets. Our version includes seven objects that were not in the original catalog. For 10 points-name this Frenchman's list of 110 stellar objects, designated by "M" numbers.

One character in this play remarks, "I Go, I go, look how I go! Swifter than an arrow from a bow!" This work features a play-within-a-play in which Peter Quince and the "rude mechanicals" perform Pyramis and Thisbe . In this play, Lysander and Hermia flee into the woods to elope. While in those woods, the trickster Puck uses love potion on various character's eyes. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy which sees Bottom turned into a Donkey, and features the fairy royals Oberon and Titania.

Hecuba laments the fall of Troy in a play titled for this kind of people. In the Greek comedy Lysistrata, the title character convinces these people to stop having sex in order to end a war. Hercules's ninth labor was to steal the girdle of Hippolyta, the leader of a group of warriors composed of these people. The Amazons were all, for 10 points, what kind of person with whom Zeus frequently cheated on his wife Hera?
acceptableAnswers: any answers indicating that they were female

tossups.text: In one organism, neurons in animals with this trait express Gustatory receptor 68a. Jonathan Hodgkin developed "high incidence" mutations in one organism to increase this trait's frequency from its 0.2% wild-type rate. In that model organism used by Horvitz and Sulston, L1 to L4 animals with this trait have a linker cell that migrates towards the cloaca ("klow-AY-kuh"). In another species, third-instar larvae with this trait have pronounced translucent discs and later develop "combs" on their front legs. Adult C. elegans with this trait have a blunt tail with a fan and rays among their 1,033 somatic cells. Adult Drosophila with this trait are smaller than their counterparts and have a darker, rounded abdomen. For 10 points, Thomas Hunt Morgan testcrossed a fly with white eyes and what sex, which is conferred in mammals by the gene SRY?
acceptableAnswers: prompt on adult until “L1” is read

tossups.text: This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for heart valves and their functions. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this atrium-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The atrium is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in heart valves and their functions.

tossups.text: The world's second-largest aquarium tank is in this city, where an oblong-shaped bright yellow Ferris wheel depicting a deity holding a penguin was recently renovated by the retail chain Don Quijote. One of this city's mascots is a mechanical drum-playing clown named after this city's culture of "eat till you drop," while others include a giant mechanical crab and a running man on a Glico billboard. A crowd in this city seeking a Randy Bass lookalike chose a Colonel Sanders statue to throw into a river, leading to a curse on the Hanshin Tigers. This city's tourist destinations include the entertainment district Dōtonbori and a castle owned by the Toyotomi clan that was besieged by Ieyasu Tokugawa. The Keihanshin metropolitan area is formed by Kobe, Kyoto, and, for 10 points, what city in the Kansai region, which after Tokyo and Yokohama is the third most populous in Japan?

In human physiology, this structure is essential for stress response. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this adrenal-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The adrenal is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in stress response.

tossups.text: One disease associated with this effect causes dwarfism, polydactyly, and occasional heart abnormalities, Ellis-van Creveld syndrome, and this effect has been blamed for an increased proportion of Huntingon's among Afrikaners. Examples of populations displaying it are the Pennsylvania Dutch and Martha's Vineyard. It often results in a non-random sample of genes and causes results similar to bottlenecking. For 10 points, name this effect causing reduced genetic variation which arises from a colony being settled by a small portion of the original population.

This continent was first discovered by the Russian ship Vostok, which is also the name of this continent's largest lake. The Amundsen Sea on the western part of this continent is usually frozen over. For 10 points, name this continent that contains the Ross Ice Shelf and is located at the South Pole.

When this quantity is calculated for gasoline at 100 degrees Fahrenheit, it is called the "Reid" type. The August-Roche-Magnus formula for this quantity is a correction of the equation for the slope of coexistence curves. Without regard to substance-specific parameters, the reciprocal of the log of this quantity equals temperature in the Antoine equation, and one form of this quantity can be estimated with the Lee-Kesler method. This quantity for a certain mixture is equal to this quantity in a pure gas multiplied by the mole fraction, according to Raoult's Law. For 10 points, name this quantity which is equal to the force that a liquid exerts on the atmosphere.

William Tubman served as president for 27 years under a party with this name, which is the oldest political party in Liberia. Lord John Russell formed a disastrous ministry that contributed to the demise of another party with this name. An American party with this name fractured into "Cotton" and "Conscience" factions, ending the "Second Party System." That party with this name elected William Henry Harrison and Zachary Taylor as president while opposing the Democrats. For 10 points, give this name shared by the American party formed to oppose Andrew Jackson and the British party that opposed the Tories.

A parable related by this person describes a deformed woman who, when giving birth, frantically looks to see if her child resembles her. In order to avoid political duties, this thinker told some messengers about a dead turtle that would rather be alive and playing in the mud. This thinker compared himself to a carpenter who used a hatchet to remove dirt from a man's nose after this man visited the grave of his friend Huizi. After his wife died, this man was observed beating a drum and singing because he believed that death was just another natural transformation. A text by this thinker describes a butcher whose knife has not worn out in nineteen years and who teaches his master to enjoy life. For 10 points, name this Daoist thinker who famously dreamt of being a butterfly.

Brandenburg v. Ohio created an "imminent lawless action" test to replace this amendment's "clear and present danger" doctrine utilized in Schenck v. US. The case Tinker v. Des Moines ruled that this amendment applies to students. The Establishment Clause of this amendment enforces the separation of church and state. Obscenity and shouting "fire" in a crowded theater are not protected by this amendment. For 10 points, name this amendment that guarantees freedom of religion and speech.

King Laomedon [lah-oh-may-don] tricked Apollo and this god into building the walls of Troy. This god cursed Pasipha¨e [pah-sih-fah-ay] after her husband, Minos, failed to sacrifice the Cretan Bull to this god. Horses were sacred to this god, who lost a competition to Athena's olive tree when he gave a salt spring to Athens. For 10 points, name this brother of Zeus and Hades, the Greek god of the sea.

In one novel by this author, a math teacher is recruited to rewrite the novel Air Chrysalis. The title character reads Richard Burton's translation of The Arabian Nights in the odd chapters of a work by this author, while the even chapters tell about a character who kills Johnnie Walker. Aomame and Tengo are transported to an alternate Earth with two moons in a novel by this author. The protagonist of one work by this author of 1Q84 [one-Q-eight-four] reminisces after hearing a cover of a Beatles song and visits Naoko in a sanatorium. For 10 points, name this author who wrote Norwegian Wood and Kafka on the Shore.

parts.text: Name this river, whose tributaries include the Missori, Arkansas, Ohio, and Red rivers. This river shares its name with a Southern state.
The Mississippi river empties into this large body of water near New Orleans.
This small lake located in Clearwater Country, Minnesota is where the Mississippi River originates. This river's name is a portmanteau of the Latin words for "truth" and "head."

bonuses.leadin: In 1811, The New Madrid Earthquake caused this river to temporarily flow backwards. For ten points each:

parts.text: Name this transaction that was agreed to on March 30th, 1867, in which the United States acquired over four hundred million acres of land from Russia for seven point two million dollars.
This Secretary of State negotiated the purchase of Alaska, which was controversial due to the seeming lack of resources in Alaska at the time; as such, the deal became known as this man's "Folly."

The purchase proved wise relatively quickly, as Alaska became the site of several of these economic booms. An 1848 one of these events started at Sutter's Mill and caused a boom in California's population.

bonuses.leadin: Great Britain was initially approached to take part in this event but declined, and the US delayed their part in this event until after the Civil War. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this director. His films, which include Rear Window, Vertigo, and Psycho, have earned him the title of Master of Suspense.

This Hitchcock film stars Cary Grant as Roger Thornhill, a man caught in the wrong place at the wrong time. Two famous scenes in this film involve Grant fleeing a crop duster and climbing Mount Rushmore.

In North by Northwest, Thornhill is mistaken for a man carrying a sensitive microfilm, a typical Hitchcockian plot device of this name. This device puts the plot in motion but serves little purpose otherwise.

bonuses.leadin: This director remade his own film The Man Who Knew Too Much, commenting that "the first version [was] the work of a talented amateur and the second was made by a professional." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this man granted a huge namesake tract of land in the American colonies between New York and Maryland, who oversaw the creation of the city of Philadelphia.
William Penn was affiliated with this religious movement led by George Fox.
Penn was granted the charter to Pennsylvania by this British monarch in repayment to debts owed by this king to Penn's father.

bonuses.leadin: After being converted to the doctrine of the "Inner Light," this man's agitations led him to be repeatedly imprisoned, where he wrote his pamphlet "No Cross, No Crown." For 10 points each:

parts.text: This ubiquitous projection, named after its 16th-century Flemish originator, stretches area near the poles to make Greenland seem larger than Brazil.

This projection was reformulated by its second namesake as a reaction against the "colonialist" Mercator projection. It privileges area accuracy over silly-looking shape distortion, stretching out Africa and South America and all but squashing the poles.

This map turns the globe into an icosahedron and unfolds it, leaving nothing properly facing upwards and, usually, the Arctic in the center. It was predictably named by its inventor, Buckminster Fuller.

bonuses.leadin: Name some cartographic projections, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this enzyme, whose membrane-bound type is the entry point of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. This enzyme is inhibited by drugs that lower blood pressure.
Angiotensin II stimulates these organs to release aldosterone. One hormone produced by these glands stimulates a "fight or flight" response.
Angiotensin is part of the RAAS system, which promotes reabsorption of this ion to the blood. Digoxins increase levels of this ion by inhibiting an ATPase which pumps three of it out of cells.

bonuses.leadin: A class of drugs inhibits this enzyme by increasing levels of bradykinin. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Margaret Atwood, an author from this country, wrote The Handmaid's Tale, in which handmaids are forced to dress in red. Some Handmaids try to flee to this country after leaving the former United States.
This poet of "This Is Just To Say" described a "a red wheel/barrow/glazed with rain/water beside the white/chickens."
Stephen Crane's novel The Red Badge of Courage, meanwhile, was set during this war. Battles during this war included Bull Run and Antietam.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer some questions about the color red in literature:

parts.text: Name this Hindu epic told by Vyasa that focuses on the Kurukshetra [koo-rook-shay-trah] war between the Kauravas [kaw-rah-vahs] and the Pandavas [pan-dah-vahs]. The Bhagavad Gita is a section of this epic work.
In the Mahabharata, this eighth avatar of the god Vishnu serves as the charioteer and companion to the Pandava prince Arjuna.

Krishna helps Arjuna marry Draupadi by giving him the opportunity to participate in a shooting contest. In the contest, Draupadi's potential husbands must shoot the eye of a moving one of these animals that swims on the ceiling, without looking at it.

bonuses.leadin: A character in this work loses his entire kingdom in a dice game. When he plays again, his entire family is forced to live in exile for twelve years. For 10 points each,

parts.text: This method works by generating random points, then determining the ratio of points inside the desired volume to points in a slightly larger domain of known volume. It can use recursive stratified sampling.
This rule, one of the Newton-Cotes formulas, works by approximating the region under the graph of a function as a namesake shape. It is usually more accurate than methods using rectangles.

This method is based on expanding the integrand in terms of Chebyshev polynomials. It substitutes the term cosine of theta for x in the integral, and then uses a discrete cosine transform approximation for the cosine series.

bonuses.leadin: Name some methods of numerical integration, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with bronchi and bronchioles.
What is the main function of the bronchus in the respiratory system?
Name another component of the respiratory system related to bronchi and bronchioles.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human respiratory system.

parts.text: Name this river which includes Moscow as part of its drainage basin, the largest river in Europe.
The Volga empties into this salty lake famous for its sturgeon population which also borders Iran to the south.

Another river which empties into the Caspian Sea is this one formerly known as the Vaik which flows through Kazakhstan to Magnitogorsk at the southern end of a namesake mountain range which encompasses Perm and Yekaterinburg.

bonuses.leadin: Astrakhan lies in its delta, while Glenn Miller and Manuel de Falla helped popularize a song about its boatmen. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with action potentials.
What is the main function of the axon in the nervous system?
Name another component of the nervous system related to action potentials.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human nervous system.

parts.text: Name this group of elements with a full outer valence ("VAY-luhns") shell.
This lightest noble gas has an atomic number of 2. This element is commonly used to fill balloons.
Potassium-40 undergoes beta-decay to form an isotope of this other noble gas, which is the third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere.

bonuses.leadin: Atoms of these elements chiefly interact via London dispersion forces. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This country's flag depicts a red circular sun on a white background. Since this country is "the Land of the Rising Sun", the sun on its flag is considered sacred.

This country's flag has a sky blue background with a grain-colored rayed sun in the center above a steppe eagle, as well as a traditional ornamental design on one edge. This country's flag was designed by Shaken Niyazbekov.

The flags of Uruguay and this neighboring country characteristically have faces. This country's flag contains two stripes of sky blue, with a sun in the central white stripe, and was designed by General Manuel Belgrano.

bonuses.leadin: Suns, often rising suns, are common symbols on national flags. Name some countries with suns on their flags, for 10 points each:

parts.text: The gas constant, symbolized by this letter, is the only other parameter in the ideal gas law. The law is often written as PV equals n times this letter times T.

This man names a terrible cubic equation of state which has two empirical parameters. He also lends his name to a set of intermolecular forces caused by both instantaneous and permanent molecular dipoles.

The Benedict-Webb-Rubin equation has eight empirical parameters, but simplifies to the ideal gas law when this quantity is small. The ideal gas law predicts this quantity equals pressure times molar mass over RT.

bonuses.leadin: You know what they say: if your model for a non-ideal gas doesn't fit, add empirical parameters until it does! For 10 points each:

parts.text: Erasing the memories of people sometimes meant re-arranging homes to disrupt the technique of "memory palaces" illustrated by this man in De Oratore. Mark Antony's wife Fulvia stabbed the tongue of this master orator.

Erasing the images of governors or emperors was often difficult because they appeared on these objects like the denarius or libra. These objects were commonly minted in silver and used to purchase in Roman forums.

After burying the Vestal Virgin Cornelia alive amongst other cruel acts, this dynasty's last member Domitian was subject to a damnatio memoriae. This dynasty arose under Vespasian after the Year of the Four Emperors.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about damnatio memoriae, or the literal erasure of public figures in ancient Rome. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this non-cognitivist position that says that ethical sentences do not state facts, but rather convey the speaker's evaluative attitudes. Emotivism is sometimes considered a form of it.
The aforementioned problem is co-named for this German author of "On Sense and Reference."

The developer of this theory, Simon Blackburn, used commitment-theoretic semantics to address the Frege-Geach problem. This theory says that ethical sentences project the speaker's attitudes as if they were statements about the world.

bonuses.leadin: According to a problem identified by Peter Geach, this position entails that the phrase "It is wrong to tell lies" means something different in the conditional "If it is wrong to tell lies, then it is wrong to get your little brother to lie." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Russian psychologist.
Pavlov's work with dogs demonstrated this type of conditioning, contrasted with operant.
Another experiment that dealt with classical conditioning was this one, in which the titular entity was conditioned to associate neutral objects, like rats, with loud noises, causing fear.

bonuses.leadin: This man's most famous experiment dealt with dogs, and it taught them to salivate at the sound of a ringing bell. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Two
Another common subject of pyramid paintings is this jackal-headed god, who weighs the hearts of the dead against the feather of Ma'at.

These people, considered to be descendants of Ra, are sometimes depicted wearing the double crown, called the pschent [p'skent]; other times, these people are shown wearing an ornate blue and gold headcloth called the nemes [NEH-mehs].

bonuses.leadin: In ancient times, Egyptians depicted their people and their pantheon in paintings within the pyramids. Answer the following about pyramid paintings, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this character titling a poem in which he is "not Prince Hamlet, nor was meant to be." At one point he wonders "do I / dare disturb the universe?" opens the poem declaring, "Let us go then, you and I."
This poet wrote "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock" along with critical essays like "Hamlet and His Problems." Most famously, he wrote the long modernist poem The Waste Land.

This NON-Eliot poem notes how "all perform their tragic play" and "though Hamlet rambles and Lear rages...[tragedy] cannot gro." It also describes "two Chinamen," "a symbol of longevity," and "a serving-man."

bonuses.leadin: This character wonders if he should "have the strength to force the moment to its crisis" after noting how "the evening sleeps so peacefully." For 10 points each:
